sources.what: INTMARB/IMP = 0.81 in 2022, 2023 and 2024; gross inland deliveries only 0.47-0.50 Mt of 2.7-2.9 Mt imports

proposals.note: Data show that 81% of Malta's imported products leave as bunkers for foreign ships. The builder still keeps 97% at the hub in the central case and subtracts bunkers only from the low end (years_lo uses hi+bunker). Proposal: in the central case also take off half of the central bunker share. Bunkers are fuel bought by foreign shipowners, not the hub's economy. 'Half' is a judgement between the current treatment (0) and full removal (1). The change applies only where bunkers are more than 75% of imports (MLT, GIB).

proposals.note: China (and Brazil, Greece, Singapore) record bunker fuel sold to foreign-flag ships as exports to the flag state. Since China refines Russian crude, these records carry laundered oil to the three largest flag registries. Dropping those partner records, or treating them as bunkers with no country buyer, removes the cause; the per-country caps above then become a backstop. The flows and the explanation are data: own vs mirror customs show the mismatch.
